key_insight: TETO uses a teacher–student knowledge distillation scheme to learn event-based motion estimation and frame interpolation from only ≈25 minutes of unlabelled real-world recordings, closing the sim-to-real gap without large synthetic datasets.
problem_solved: Event-based motion estimators typically rely on large synthetic datasets, producing a significant sim-to-real gap and requiring costly annotations—TETO enables accurate real-world event motion learning with minimal unlabelled data.
method: Teacher–student framework: an RGB-based teacher provides supervisory signals from sparse frames while a student network learns to track raw event streams.
Knowledge distillation on real unannotated recordings (~25 minutes) to transfer motion and interpolation cues from the teacher to the event-based student.
Losses and temporal alignment encourage event-driven motion estimation and frame interpolation consistency without synthetic pretraining or dense labels.
impact: Reduces dependence on synthetic labels and large annotated datasets, enabling robust event-camera motion estimation and high-quality frame interpolation from small amounts of real data—useful for robotics, autonomous driving, and efficient video processing.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing RGB teacher supervising an event-based student (inputs: frames + event stream → outputs: motion field and interpolated frames).
Before/after frame interpolation comparison (RGB ground truth vs student interpolated frames) to illustrate visual improvement.
Timeline visualization comparing high-rate event stream (microsecond resolution) with sparse RGB frames to show complementary modalities.
Bar chart or dot plot showing performance vs training data type/amount (synthetic large dataset vs TETO on ≈25 minutes real data).
paper_title: TETO: Tracking Events with Teacher Observation for Motion Estimation and Frame Interpolation
paper_authors: Jini Yang, Eunbeen Hong, Soowon Son, Hyunkoo Lee, Sunghwan Hong
